chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about something of the expiation of an oath. He said, 'He fasts for three days.' I said, 'If he is weak from fasting and unable to do so,' he said, 'He gives charity to ten poor people.' I said, 'If he is unable to do that,' he said, 'Then let him seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted, and not repeat [the oath].'
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step expiation for breaking an oath according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the tripartite hierarchy of kaffarah for breaking an oath, a ruling derived from Quran 66:1 but clarified by Imam al-Sadiq to address practical limitations. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of progressive ease (tadarruj), where the final tier of 'seeking forgiveness and resolving not to repeat' serves as a valid alternative when material capacity for fasting or feeding is absent, emphasizing spiritual intent over ritual burden.
